# .github/ci-constraints.txt — the versions CI installs.
#
# Why this file exists
# --------------------
# On 2026-09-03 the whole matrix went red without a matching code change.
# `pyproject.toml` allows `fastapi>=0.110,<1.0`; CI resolved 0.141.1, in which
# `include_router` stopped flattening routes into `app.routes`. The application
# was fine -- a workflow assertion that read a FastAPI internal was not. Nothing
# pinned the resolved version, so the break arrived on an unrelated push and had
# to be diagnosed from scratch.
#
# Every CI job now installs with `-c .github/ci-constraints.txt`, so a given
# commit resolves to the same versions today and in six months. A dependency
# upgrade becomes a commit that changes this file, reviewed and bisectable like
# any other, instead of an event that happens to whoever pushes next.
#
# The bounds in pyproject.toml stay as they are: they say what the project
# *supports*, which is a different claim from what CI *installs*. Do not narrow
# them to imitate this file.
#
# Scope
# -----
# CI only. This is not a supported install path for researchers or for the
# packaged application -- those follow pyproject.toml. It carries no hashes,
# because a constraints file with hashes requires hashes for everything in the
# install, and the editable `-e .` of this project cannot have one.
#
# The environment markers are load-bearing: one file covers all six legs of the
# matrix (ubuntu/windows x 3.10/3.11/3.12), which is why it is resolved with
# `--universal` rather than on one machine.
#
# What keeps it from going stale
# ------------------------------
# .github/workflows/dependency-canary.yml runs weekly *without* these
# constraints, against whatever PyPI offers that day, and opens an issue when
# that fails. So this file being old is a tracked, visible state rather than a
# silent one.
#
# Regenerate
# ----------
#     uv pip compile --universal --python-version 3.10 --extra dev \
#         --no-annotate --no-header pyproject.toml -o .github/ci-constraints.txt
#
# Then run the suite before committing the result. Bumping the pins is a change
# to what CI proves, and deserves the same evidence as a change to the code.
